content:
All rotations/reflections of the 4-cell L are exactly the three-cell subsets of a \(2\times2\) square. Thus, if any \(2\times2\) block had at most one colored cell, the other three cells would form an uncolored L. So every \(2\times2\) block must have at least 2 colored cells.

Partition the \(6\times6\) board into nine disjoint \(2\times2\) blocks. Each requires at least 2 colored cells, giving at least \(9\cdot 2=18\) colored cells.

A checkerboard coloring uses exactly 18 cells, and every \(2\times2\) block has 2 colored cells, so every L placement contains a colored cell.

\[
\boxed{18}
\]
